document.abstract: The absence of any camera movement in composited images often undermines the credibility of the composite or gives the images an awkward quality. To overcome this limitation a portable, computerized pan/tilt head capable of repeating pans, tilts, zooms and focus pulls with the accuracy required for image compositing has been developed. It can be operated in the same way as a conventional fluid head tripod, or it can be remotely controlled by a variety of means.

authors.bio: Richard Patterson has been director of marketing for Ultimatte Corp. since 1986. From 1985 to 1986 he was general manager of Ruxton, Ltd. He was editor and business manager of American Cinematographer from 1981 to 1985, and from 1970 to 1981 he was a free-lance film producer, director, and editor. Patterson has a B.A. degree from Yale University.
